\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Switching Bernoulli}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.SwitchingBernoulli
\section{Overview}

This module proves the Bernoulli version of Håstad's switching lemma for
decision-tree depth: under a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction with $p \le 1/(40w)$,
a width-$w$ DNF (or CNF) has restricted decision-tree depth exceeding $t$ with
probability at most $(1/2)^t + e^{-np/3}$. It is derived by bridging from the
fixed-size counting switching lemma to the Bernoulli restriction model.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality of fixed-size restrictions]
\lean{SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_card}
\label{SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_card}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.numSRestrictions}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k \le n$. Among all restrictions on $n$
variables — maps assigning each variable either a fixed Boolean value or leaving it free
— those whose set of free variables has cardinality exactly $k$ number precisely
$\binom{n}{k}\,2^{\,n-k}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Equal counts of the bad size-$k$ restrictions]
\lean{SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_filter_bad_eq}
\label{SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_filter_bad_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, SwitchingLemma2.IsBadRestriction, SwitchingLemma2.IsRestriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.numFree, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables and fix natural numbers $d$ and $k$. For
a restriction $\rho$ on these variables, write $f|_\rho$ for the restricted function
that sends a point $x$ to the value of $f$ obtained by fixing each assigned coordinate
as $\rho$ prescribes and reading each free coordinate off $x$, and call $\rho$ bad for
$f$ at depth $d$ when the decision-tree depth of $f|_\rho$ is strictly greater than $d$.
Then the number of restrictions that have exactly $k$ free variables and are bad for $f$
at depth $d$ is the same whether these are counted within the collection of all
restrictions with exactly $k$ free variables or within the collection of all
restrictions on the $n$ variables that both have exactly $k$ free variables and are bad
for $f$ at depth $d$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrs, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_card, SwitchingBernoulli.fixedSizeRestrs_filter_bad_eq, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction.freeVars, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, SwitchingLemma2.switching_lemma, dtDepth}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables with $n \ge 1$, and suppose every term
of $f$ has width at most $w$, so that $f$ is a disjunction of conjunctions of at most
$w$ literals. Assume that no variable occurs more than once within any single term, that
is, each term consists of literals with pairwise distinct variables (and hence has no
repeated literal). Fix natural numbers $k$ and $d$ with $5k \le n$, and draw a
restriction $\rho$ uniformly at random from the fixed-size model $R_k$, which is uniform
over all restrictions of the $n$ variables that leave exactly $k$ variables free. Then
the probability that the restricted function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has
decision-tree depth greater than $d$ satisfies
\[
\bbP_{\rho \sim R_k}\!\bigl[\, \mathrm{depth}\bigl(f\!\restriction_\rho\bigr) > d
\,\bigr] \;\le\; \left(\frac{10\,k\,w}{n}\right)^{d},
\]
where $\mathrm{depth}(g)$ denotes the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Switching lemma for fixed-size restrictions]

  {SwitchingBernoulli.switching_fixedSize_bound_small}

\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb_le_one, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_fixedSize_bound_small, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables in which every term has width at most
$w$, where $w \ge 1$, and in which each term is reduced: no literal is repeated, and any
two literals of a term sharing the same variable are equal (so a variable occurs at most
once, and never with both polarities, within a term). For a Boolean function $g$ on some
set of inputs, write $D(g)$ for its decision-tree depth, the least depth of a decision
tree computing $g$. Fix a natural number $d$ and an integer $k$ with $k \le n$, and draw
a restriction $\rho$ uniformly at random among all restrictions of the $n$ variables
that leave exactly $k$ variables free (the fixed-size restriction model $R_k$). Writing
$f|_\rho$ for the function obtained by fixing each set variable to the value assigned by
$\rho$ and keeping the $k$ free variables as inputs, one has
\[
\bbP_{\rho}\!\left[\, D(f|_\rho) > d \,\right] \;\le\;
\left(\frac{10\,k\,w}{n}\right)^{d}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\proofstep
  {SwitchingBernoulli.switching_fixedSize_bound}
  {direct}
  {switching-lemma}
  {pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008}
\uses{BernoulliCost.fixedSizeRestrProb, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_fixedSize_bound, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{2}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$, with
$w \ge 1$, and suppose that within each term of $f$ no variable occurs more than once —
that is, every term is a repetition-free list of literals in which any two literals
sharing a variable are identical. Fix an integer $k$ with $0 \le k \le n$, and let $R_k$
denote the fixed-size restriction model, uniform over all restrictions of the $n$
variables that leave exactly $k$ of them free. Then for every $d$, the probability under
$R_k$ that the restricted function $f_\rho$ (with the assigned coordinates fixed
according to $\rho$ and the $k$ free coordinates left as inputs) has decision-tree depth
greater than $d$ satisfies
\[ \bbP_{\rho \sim R_k}\!\left[\, \mathrm{depth}(f_\rho) > d \,\right] \;\le\; \left(\frac{5k \cdot 2w}{n}\right)^{d}. \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli switching lemma for DNF formulas]
\lean{SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008}
\label{SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\uses{BernoulliCost.bernoulli_restriction_cost, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_fixedSize_bound_rescaled, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb_le_one', SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ Boolean variables whose width is at most $w$,
where $w \ge 1$, and suppose that no term of $f$ reads any variable more than once: each
term is a duplicate-free list of literals, and any two literals in a common term that
share a variable are equal. Fix a real parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, so
in particular $p \le 1$. Then for every $t \in \bbn$, under a Bernoulli($p$) random
restriction $\rho$ the restricted function $f\vert_\rho$ (that is, $f$ evaluated on the
free coordinates with the remaining coordinates fixed by $\rho$) satisfies
\[
\Pr_{p}\big[\, f\vert_\rho \text{ has decision-tree depth exceeding } t \,\big] \;\le\;
\left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right),
\]
where the decision-tree depth of a Boolean function is the least depth of a decision
tree computing it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli switching lemma for CNF formulas]
\lean{SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008}
\label{SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF.eval, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, SwitchingLemmaCNF.cnfToDualDNF_inj, SwitchingLemmaCNF.cnfToDualDNF_nodup, cnfToDualDNF, cnfToDualDNF_eval, cnfToDualDNF_width, dtDepth, dtDepth_neg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a CNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge
1$, and suppose every clause of $f$ is proper: within any one clause, two literals
sharing the same variable are equal, and no literal is repeated. Let $p \in \bbr$
satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, and in addition $p \le 1$. Draw a Bernoulli($p$)
random restriction $\rho$, which independently leaves each variable free with
probability $p$ and otherwise fixes it to one of the two Boolean values, each with
probability $(1-p)/2$; write $f\vert_\rho$ for the function of the remaining free
variables obtained by fixing the assigned coordinates according to $\rho$. Then for
every $t \in \bbn$,
\[
  \Pr_\rho\big[\,\mathrm{depth}(f\vert_\rho) > t\,\big]
    \;\le\; \left(\tfrac12\right)^{t} + e^{-np/3},
\]
where $\mathrm{depth}(g)$ denotes the least depth of a decision tree computing $g$.
\end{theorem}
